answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 24% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the juniper balance is debited each close, the signal ledger exposes the bleed, and the meadow audit lists every fee. An operator holding 189 idle keys thus pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
